subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should managed npm plugin projects continue inheriting all OpenClaw host dependency overrides, or should core scope/filter those overrides so plugin-owned dependency graphs like Express 4 can resolve their own transitive versions?
rationale: Both plausible fixes change the plugin dependency ownership boundary: filtering overrides affects security/reproducibility policy, while a central downgrade conflicts with core's Express 5/router stack.

options.title: Scope Managed Overrides
options.body: Preserve OpenClaw root pins for core, filter or namespace managed-root overrides for third-party plugin projects, and add regression coverage for an Express 4 plugin install.

options.title: Validator Only
options.body: Keep override propagation unchanged but detect Express 4/path-to-regexp conflicts and fail with an actionable plugin-author message.

options.title: Plugin-Owned Fix Only
options.body: Leave OpenClaw core unchanged and require affected plugins to ship their own override, shrinkwrap, bundled dependency, or Express 5 migration.

recommendation.title: Scope Managed Overrides
recommendation.body: Preserve OpenClaw root pins for core, filter or namespace managed-root overrides for third-party plugin projects, and add regression coverage for an Express 4 plugin install.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent history ties this login to managed override metadata and the broader plugin install/security surface, which is the policy boundary in question.
